business_problem: Elevance Health needed to find fraud, waste, and abuse in very large volumes of claims, payment, contract, and medical-record data so it could detect billing errors, suspicious coding patterns, and improper payments earlier while controlling healthcare costs and protecting program integrity.
solution_summary: Elevance Health describes an in-house AI-assisted payment integrity workflow that combines predictive AI, AI-driven lead identification, and human review inside Carelon’s Payment Integrity operation. The process starts with claims and payment data, which models analyze to determine whether services were billed and paid appropriately and to surface unusual coding or charging patterns relative to peers or local norms. Supporting AI-powered programs also summarize thousands of pages of medical records and align formatting across care provider contract data and medical claims so auditors can review suspected irregularities faster. The outputs are not used autonomously: investigators, auditors, and the Special Investigations Unit review flagged leads, interpret whether anomalies stem from mistakes, contract differences, regulations, or intentional upcoding, and then decide on education, recovery, termination, or other follow-up actions.
data_flow: Claims and payment data are analyzed by predictive AI models to flag unusual billing patterns, while AI-powered programs process medical records and normalize care provider contract and claims formats. These outputs flow to Payment Integrity investigators, auditors, and the Special Investigations Unit, who review the evidence, determine whether fraud, waste, or abuse is occurring, and take follow-up action.
business_outcome: Elevance Health says AI helps investigators identify issues earlier in the claims process, speeds audits and medical-record review, improves the efficiency of fraud, waste, and abuse investigations, and supports cost control and healthcare program integrity.
metrics: from an average of 40 minutes to 20 minutes
across an annualized volume of nearly 23,000 reviews
